milestone: Whole-record lexical captures in synchronous native CPU numeric callbacks

implementation.capture_types: Completed immutable CPU records, including finite nested records and numeric collection fields
implementation.typing: Preserve nominal declaration identity through lifted callback parameters; reject same-layout sibling capture substitution
implementation.lowering: Reuse existing callback function lifting, CPU LLVM aggregate arguments and continuation helper imports
implementation.ownership: Reuse existing record collection packing/read copies and recursive worker retention; no runtime or checked-ABI changes
implementation.scope: Synchronous numeric scalar callbacks only; referenced lexical bindings deduplicated and propagated through nested callbacks

coverage: Six CPU numeric families; signed zero, infinities, NaN payloads and raw integer bits
Borrowed strided inputs unchanged, retained outputs after invocation settlement and allocation-failure sweeps
Nested scalar/Bool/array/tensor record fields captured in direct calls and pipelines
Nested closures, repeated binding deduplication and parameter shadowing
Completed worker records captured by subsequent direct/nested worker maps
Immutable record updates inside callbacks; originals unchanged
Imported inferred nominal record values with aliased helper calls
Empty maps do not evaluate a failing callback; nonempty faults keep source location
Cached observations, cancellation, deadlines, task admission and task/invocation allocation failure
Malformed capture declaration identity and incomplete task/fallible captures rejected
Executable documentation example and prior compiler/map/closure/record/module/worker/selected Metal regressions
qualification.scope: Focused qualification, not the full registered suite

boundaries: Record-valued map results and arrays of records remain pending
Callbacks remain synchronous throughout their helper graph
No escaping closures or general first-class function ABI
Shared-storage and earlier record backing reclamation remain optimization follow-ups
